Evaluate if partner response demonstrates applicable areas (not required for all) such as Data Privacy compliance, data leakage prevention measures, data access controls and activity logs used, privacy impact assessments conducted.

Evaluate if partner describes implementations such as content moderation policies, fact-checking procedures.
Evaluate if Partners describes a processes that prevent the generation of plagiarized or copyrighted content.
Evaluate if partner response describes the model customization process (prerequisites, data preparation, model training, results validation, new model use, common issues, and best practices).

Evaluate if partner has implemented a system to track and manage security issues. PASS if submission demonstrates use of a ticketing or tracking system to manage security-related issues, system allows tracking of security concerns with basic ownership assignment, system captures security issues reported about the solution. FAIL if no system exists for tracking security issues, no process for managing security concerns, no way to track or assign ownership of security issues.

Evaluate if the solution uses official AWS tools or SDKs for AWS API calls with appropriate error handling. PASS if partner uses official AWS tools (such as AWS SDK, AWS CLI, or infrastructure tools like Terraform) for API calls, or mentions implementation of retry logic with exponential backoff and jitter. FAIL if partner explicitly mentions using unofficial or third-party SDKs, or provides no information about AWS API interaction methods.

Evaluate if the partner has measures to prevent AWS API throttling in customer accounts. PASS if submission demonstrates any rate limiting, bandwidth controls, or throttling prevention measures for AWS services, including but not limited to API call rate limiting, bandwidth limiting for data operations, or other mechanisms that help prevent service throttling. FAIL if no throttling prevention measures are mentioned or partner explicitly states they make unlimited API calls without any controls.

Evaluate if the partner solution avoids unnecessary polling of AWS control plane APIs. PASS if submission demonstrates the solution does not rely on polling AWS APIs for status checks, uses AWS native services (such as AutoScaling groups, load balancer health checks, CloudTrail, EventBridge, or AWS Config) for monitoring and state management, or describes alternative methods to avoid frequent API polling. FAIL if solution explicitly relies on continuous polling of AWS control plane APIs without any alternative mechanisms or throttling controls.

PASS if submission shows ANY of: (1) Specific KPI metrics listed (latency, uptime, error rate, etc.), (2) Performance thresholds defined with numbers (e.g., <100ms latency), (3) Monitoring approach described (CloudWatch, Datadog, custom dashboards), (4) Customer-facing performance metrics tracked. FAIL if only says 'we monitor performance' without specific metrics, thresholds, or monitoring tools.

Evaluate if the partner conducts performance test suites before major releases or production deployments to ensure new versions meets performance targets. PASS if submission mentions performance test suites either automated or manual are run before major releases or production deployments to ensure new versions meet performance targets. FAIL if partner lacks performance tests before releases or deployments or no integration with CI/CD pipeline

Evaluate if partner performs peer-to-peer code reviews before each release or deployment. PASS if submission demonstrates or mentions that peer-to-peer code reviews are conducted as part of the development or release process. FAIL if no code review process is mentioned or partner explicitly states they do not conduct peer reviews.

Evaluate if automated functional test suites exist and automatically run before software release or deployment to production ensuring functionality and preventing regressions. PASS if submission demonstrates automated functional test suites exist and are automatically run before software is released or deployed to production, or mentions use of automation and CI/CD frameworks that include testing as part of the release process. FAIL if lacks any automated testing, missing automatic execution before release or deployment, or no mention of testing frameworks or automation in release process.

PASS if partner uses issue tracking tool (Jira, GitHub Issues, Linear, ServiceNow, etc.) to manage backlogs, feature requests, OR defects. Tool must be named or described. FAIL if no tracking tool mentioned or only uses email/spreadsheets without formal system.

Evaluate if the partner establishes process to track and remediate customer reported product bugs and operational incidents. PASS if submission demonstrates process established to track and remediate customer reported product bugs and operational incidents, or describes a system for capturing and managing customer issues including bugs and incidents through appropriate tracking tools. FAIL if lacks any issue tracking process or no system mentioned for handling customer reported issues.

Evaluate if partner automatically detects and alerts on anomalous activity based on AWS CloudTrail logs using automated tools such as Amazon GuardDuty and integrates alerting with security issue tracking system. PASS if partner has AWS CloudTrail logs actively monitored using automated tools such as Amazon GuardDuty to detect suspicious or anomalous behavior. FAIL if lacks active monitoring of CloudTrail logs using automated tools or integration with security ticketing system.

Evaluate if partner automatically detects and alerts on anomalous network activity for production using automated tools with alerting mechanisms. PASS if submission demonstrates network activity actively monitored using automated tools such as Amazon GuardDuty to detect suspicious or anomalous behavior, and alerting configured to notify security or operations teams when suspicious behaviors detected. FAIL if lacks active monitoring of network activity, missing automated tools for suspicious behavior detection, or no alerting mechanism described.

Evaluate if partner implements infrastructure configuration policies and monitors compliance using automated tooling. PASS if submission mentions use of configuration policies for AWS infrastructure or automated tooling such as AWS Config for monitoring compliance. FAIL if no mention of configuration policies or automated compliance monitoring tools.

Evaluate if partner uses certificate management system to maintain SSL/TLS certificates with automated mechanisms to prevent certificates from expiring unexpectedly. PASS if submission mentions use of certificate management system such as AWS Certificate Manager or similar tools for SSL/TLS certificates, or describes automated mechanisms to prevent certificate expiration. FAIL if no certificate management system mentioned or no automated expiration prevention described.

Evaluate if partner models tenant identity in software layer for multi-tenant components with controls ensuring tenant isolation. PASS if submission mentions tenant identity modeling in software layer, describes tenant isolation approach, or indicates awareness of preventing cross-tenant data access. FAIL if no mention of tenant identity modeling or tenant isolation for shared infrastructure.

Evaluate whether partner deploys single-tenant components to tenant-specific Amazon VPCs or describes tenant isolation approach. PASS if submission mentions deployment of single-tenant components to tenant-specific VPCs, describes VPC-per-tenant model for components not designed for multi-tenant software isolation, or indicates use of separate compute resources and network isolation per tenant. FAIL if no mention of tenant-specific VPCs, shared infrastructure without tenant isolation described, or no approach to tenant separation at infrastructure level.

Evaluate if single-tenant components use dedicated IAM roles per tenant with policies limiting access to tenant-specific resources. PASS if submission demonstrates or mentions use of dedicated IAM roles per tenant, roles limit access to tenant resources using Resource and Condition statements or similar access controls, description of tenant-specific roles, or example of IAM policies providing resource isolation. FAIL if no mention of dedicated IAM roles per tenant, missing tenant-specific access controls, or no approach described for limiting access to tenant resources.

Evaluate if partner established highly available network connectivity. Network connectivity to the solution must be highly available. If using VPN or Direct Connect to connect to customer networks, the solution must support redundant connections, even if the customers do not always implement this. PASS if partner says they established highly available network connectivity or if they are using VPN or Direct Connect to connect to customer networks they have redundant connectivity. FAIL if no explicit mention of having highly available network connectivity.

Evaluate if partner continuously monitors workload health and implements alerting on any issues. PASS if submission demonstrates monitoring of system components with defined thresholds and alerting. FAIL if no monitoring or alerting mentioned.

Evaluate if partner manages AWS and application logs centrally. PASS if submission demonstrates or mentions consolidation of log information from application and AWS infrastructure into a single system, describes centralized logging approach, or indicates use of log aggregation tools or services. FAIL if no mention of centralized logging, logs are explicitly stated to be managed separately, or no log consolidation approach described.

Evaluate if application and AWS infrastructure are monitored centrally with alarms generated and sent to appropriate operations staff. PASS if submission demonstrates or mentions centralized monitoring of application and AWS infrastructure, alarms generated and sent to operations staff, or describes monitoring approach with alerting to appropriate teams. FAIL if no centralized monitoring mentioned, missing alarm generation or notification to operations staff, or no monitoring approach described.

Evaluate if solution uses automated tools like CloudFormation or Terraform to provision and manage AWS infrastructure avoiding AWS Management Console for routine production changes. PASS if submission mentions or describes solution uses automated tools such as AWS CloudFormation, Terraform, or CDK to provision and manage AWS infrastructure, avoids AWS Management Console for routine production changes, and describes infrastructure-as-code practices with version control. FAIL if submission shows complete reliance on AWS Management Console for production infrastructure changes, no mention of infrastructure automation tools, or no infrastructure-as-code practices.

Evaluate if the partner has automated code and configuration deployments. PASS if submission mentions or describes automated methods for deploying code and configuration to AWS infrastructure and avoids interactive SSH or RDP sessions for updates. FAIL if submission shows reliance on manual SSH or RDP sessions for code and configuration deployments or no mention of automated deployment methods.

Evaluate if partner has developed runbooks. PASS if submission mentions or describes runbooks that document routine operational tasks and troubleshooting scenarios, provide step-by-step instructions for activities and issue resolution, and are accessible to relevant personnel. FAIL if submission shows no mention of operational runbooks or documented procedures for routine tasks and troubleshooting.

PASS if submission mentions IMDSv2, HttpTokens=required, or EC2 metadata security configuration. If solution does not use EC2, partner must state No EC2 used. FAIL if uses EC2 but no mention of IMDSv2 enforcement OR explicitly uses IMDSv1.
